summary.text: Betty McCollum is the Democratic incumbent in Minnesota's 4th Congressional District, covering Saint Paul, Ramsey County and most of Washington County, which she has represented since 2001. A former teacher and city council member, she served in the Minnesota House before her election to Congress in 2000. She is the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee and the dean of Minnesota's congressional delegation.

paragraphs.text: Betty McCollum was born in 1954 in Minneapolis, Minnesota, grew up in South St. Paul, graduated from South St. Paul High School, and earned a B.A. from the College of St. Catherine in St. Paul.
According to her House website, she taught high school social science and worked 25 years in retail sales and management before and alongside elected service.
McCollum served on the North St. Paul City Council from 1987 to 1992.
She then served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 1993 to 2000 and was elected Assistant Leader three times by her Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party colleagues.

McCollum was elected to the U.S. House on November 7, 2000, defeating Linda Runbeck (R), Tom Foley (I) and Nicholas Skrivanek (C), and has been re-elected since; her House website says she was the second Minnesota woman elected to Congress.

She serves on the House Appropriations Committee, chairing its Defense Subcommittee in the 117th Congress and serving as its top Democrat in the 119th Congress, and she also serves on the Interior and Environment Subcommittee.
She is the dean of the Minnesota congressional delegation, the mother of two adult children, and a resident of Saint Paul, according to her House website.
